sourceEnglish.title: Mediate Two Friends' Pre-Trek Breakfast Argument
sourceEnglish.objective: Report each friend's position fairly, add the staff's facts, and help the group agree on one plan.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are the friend in the middle, and the AI plays Ana, Lars and Wilber from the hostel: report each friend's position fairly with dijo que and decía que plus the imperfect, add Wilber's facts about the market, and help everyone agree on one plan.
englishWordAnchors: Ana said she wanted to try the hen broth at the market.
Lars was saying there wasn't time before the pickup.
Wilber, could you tell me what time the market opens?
Wilber explained to us that the market opened at 6.
Listen, you both have a point.
Lars, you were saying the pickup was at 7, right?
What if we go to the market and come back before 7?
So it's settled: a quick market trip and backpacks ready beforehand.
englishGrammarExamples: Ana said she wanted to have breakfast at the market.
Lars was saying there wasn't time before the trek.
englishReading: It was 5 in the early morning in Cusco, and my friends Ana and Lars were arguing before the trek.
We were in the hostel kitchen, where Wilber, the person in charge, was making a hot emoliente.
Ana said she wanted to try the hen broth at the market.
She was also saying that the chuta bread at the San Pedro market was famous and that she didn't want to leave Cusco without trying it.
Lars was saying there wasn't time before the pickup.
His position was that the hostel's quinoa was enough and that rushing around with altitude sickness before a long trek was a bad idea.
I stepped into the middle and told them: Listen, you both have a point.
Then I asked Lars: Lars, you were saying the pickup was at 7, right?
Lars checked the agency's message and confirmed that the pickup time was at 7 at the hostel door.
Then I asked Wilber: Wilber, could you tell me what time the market opens?
Wilber explained to us that the market opened at 6.
He added that, after the opening, the broth stalls filled up quickly and that the market was a 10-minute walk away.
Wilber also said that coca tea helped many travelers with altitude sickness, so he served each of us a cup.
With that information, I proposed a middle ground: What if we go to the market and come back before 7?
Ana agreed to come back at 6:45, and Lars said he was on board if we left our backpacks ready at the front desk.
To close the agreement, I summed it up out loud: So it's settled: a quick market trip and backpacks ready beforehand.
Ana smiled, Lars finished his emoliente, and we headed out to San Pedro at 6 sharp.

lessons.title: Mediate a group breakfast plan before pickup
lessons.objective: Report two friends' preferences fairly, verify the market's opening and pickup time, then agree on a breakfast plan without rushing anyone who feels unwell.
lessons.focus: ～と言っていました reports a person's position; 一方で contrasts two positions; ～なら introduces a compromise. 高山病 is altitude sickness, コカ茶 is coca tea, and ～と話しました reports the host's statement.
lessons.scene: At a mountain lodge, two friends disagree about visiting a morning market before a scheduled shuttle pickup.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: 美咲さんは朝市で朝食を食べたいと言っていました。
reader.en: Misaki said she wanted to eat breakfast at the morning market.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: 一方で、ルカさんは送迎車に遅れるのを心配しています。
reader.en: On the other hand, Luca is worried about missing the shuttle.

reader.speaker: Luca
reader.ja: 集合時刻は七時だと思います。まず予約の連絡を確認しましょう。
reader.en: I think pickup is at seven. Let's check the booking message first.

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: 連絡には、宿の前に七時集合と書いてあります。
reader.en: The message says to meet outside the lodge at seven.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: 朝市の開店時刻と、宿からの距離も確認できますか。
reader.en: Could we check the market opening time and distance from the lodge too?

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: 六時に開きますが、混み具合は分かりません。
reader.en: It opens at six, but I do not know how crowded it will be.

reader.speaker: Misaki
reader.ja: 体調がよくない人がいたら、無理をしないほうがいいですね。
reader.en: If someone feels unwell, we should not push them.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: では、先に荷物を用意して、全員の体調を聞きましょう。
reader.en: Then let's prepare our bags first and ask how everyone feels.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: 時間と体調に余裕があるなら朝市へ、なければ宿で食べるのはどうですか。
reader.en: If we have enough time and everyone feels well, how about the market; otherwise, we can eat at the lodge?

reader.speaker: Luca
reader.ja: その条件なら賛成です。出発前にもう一度時刻を確認しましょう。
reader.en: I agree on those conditions. Let's check the time again before leaving.

reader.speaker: Mediator
reader.ja: 宿の方は、高山病にコカ茶が役立ったと言う旅行者が多いと話しました。
reader.en: The host said many travelers reported that coca tea helped with altitude sickness.

speaking.partnerRole: Two travelers and a lodging host
speaking.opening: お二人の意見を整理しましょう。まず集合時刻を確認します。
speaking.goal: Report each friend's position fairly, ask the host about market and pickup times, relay the host's statement about coca tea, and negotiate a breakfast plan.
speaking.closure: Summarize the agreed meeting and breakfast plan back to the group.

modes.see: Read a mediated group decision with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall each friend's view and verified schedule facts.
modes.hear: Hear reported speech and contrasting positions.
modes.type: Type a conditional compromise with kana support.
modes.say: Mediate the group without promising a rushed trip.
modes.write: Write a balanced summary and conditional plan.

sourceEnglish.title: Keep a Tired Group Going at a Dawn Lodge Breakfast
sourceEnglish.objective: Encourage a sleepy, cranky group, commit to a clear plan, and keep spirits up while the bread finishes.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are the group's organizer, and the AI plays cook Mirta and your sleepy companions Noor, Felipe and Greta: encourage them, commit to tasks with the future (me encargaré, saldremos), and keep spirits up with ¡vamos! and dale while the bread finishes.
englishWordAnchors: I'll take care of the thermos and the yerba.
Come on, we'll still leave on time!
Felipe, relax, the bread will be ready in a little while.
Mirta, roughly how much longer does the bread need?
Noor, can you put the packed lunches together while we wait?
Greta, I'll make you a mate while the bread bakes.
We'll get to the trail before sunrise, you'll see.
Come on, guys, the day is going to be beautiful.
englishGrammarExamples: I'll take care of the thermos and you the packed lunches.
Come on, we'll get to the trail before sunrise!
englishReading: At 5 in the morning, Sam and his companions Noor, Felipe and Greta are having breakfast at a lodge in El Chaltén before heading out to hike.
Mirta, the cook, takes the kettle off the stove and lets them know that the homemade bread needs more time in the oven.
Sam: Mirta, roughly how much longer does the bread need?
Mirta: About 20 minutes, but in the meantime you can eat the pastries with dulce de leche.
Felipe is in a bad mood because he wanted to leave right away, and he says they are going to miss the sunrise.
Sam: Felipe, relax, the bread will be ready in a little while.
Sam: We'll get to the trail before sunrise, you'll see.
Sam calmly explains the plan for the day: they will leave at 6, hike 2 hours to the lagoon and come back to the lodge in the afternoon.
Sam: I'll take care of the thermos and the yerba.
Sam: Noor, can you put the packed lunches together while we wait?
Noor yawns, but she fills each packed lunch with cheese and fruit and leaves room for the bread.
Greta is cold and can't find her jacket or her headlamp.
Felipe, calmer now, tells her: Greta, both things are in your backpack.
Sam: Greta, I'll make you a mate while the bread bakes.
With the hot mate and the pastries, the group's spirits improve a lot.
Mirta takes the homemade bread out of the oven and tells the group: It's ready, guys, the trailhead is a 10-minute walk away.
Sam: Come on, we'll still leave on time!
Sam: Come on, guys, the day is going to be beautiful.

lessons.title: Keep a tired group organized at dawn
lessons.objective: Encourage a sleepy group, divide preparation tasks, and agree on a realistic departure plan while breakfast is delayed.
lessons.focus: ～を担当します assigns a task; 出発前に means before departure; ～てから sequences a decision after checking. 無理をせず means without pushing too hard.
lessons.scene: At a hiking lodge, bread is still baking and the group shares tasks while the cook confirms when breakfast will be ready.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: パンはまだ焼いています。あと十五分ほどかかる予定です。
reader.en: The bread is still baking. It is expected to take about fifteen more minutes.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。正確な時間が分かったら教えてください。
reader.en: Thank you. Please tell us when you know the exact time.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 眠くて、出発の準備がまだ終わっていません。
reader.en: I am sleepy, and I have not finished getting ready to leave.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 無理をせず、一つずつ準備しましょう。私は水筒を担当します。
reader.en: Let's get ready one thing at a time without pushing too hard. I will take care of the thermos.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 美咲さんは持ち帰りの昼食を確認してくれますか。
reader.en: Misaki, could you check the packed lunches?

reader.speaker: Misaki
reader.ja: はい。人数と中身を確認しておきます。
reader.en: Yes. I will check the count and contents.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 出発前に上着とヘッドライトも確認しましょう。
reader.en: Let's check our jackets and headlamps before leaving too.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 天気予報と登山口までの道も見ておきます。
reader.en: I will also check the weather forecast and route to the trailhead.

reader.speaker: Cook
reader.ja: パンが焼けました。熱いので、受け取るときは気をつけてください。
reader.en: The bread is ready. It is hot, so please take care when receiving it.

reader.speaker: Organizer
reader.ja: 全員の体調と準備を確認してから、出発時刻を決めましょう。
reader.en: Let's decide when to leave after checking everyone's condition and readiness.

speaking.role: Group organizer at a hiking lodge
speaking.opening: パンはあと何分ぐらいかかりますか。待つ間に準備を分担しましょう。
speaking.goal: Ask for an updated breakfast time, assign two preparation tasks, encourage the group, and confirm readiness before departure.
speaking.closure: Do not promise arrival before sunrise or ignore weather, route or a companion's condition.

modes.see: Read a realistic dawn-preparation scene with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall the delay and assigned tasks.
modes.hear: Hear task commitments and timing language.
modes.type: Type a task assignment with kana support.
modes.say: Coordinate the group while checking readiness.
modes.write: Write a short task list and departure condition.

sourceEnglish.title: Usted or Tú: Coach a Friend at a Casa Particular
sourceEnglish.objective: Explain when to switch between usted and tú, then model it with the host, her grandson and an older guest.
sourceEnglish.speaking: You are coaching your friend Marcus, and the AI plays Marcus, host señora Odalys, her grandson Yandiel and guest don Rigoberto: explain when to use usted or tú, then model each with softeners like quisiera, ¿me podría…? and ¿te importa…?
englishWordAnchors: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.
You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.
englishGrammarExamples: Señora Odalys, could you pass me the coffee pot, please?
Yandiel, do you mind if I sit here?
englishReading: Lucía and her friend Marcus are having breakfast on the front porch of a casa particular in Trinidad, Cuba.
The host, señora Odalys, puts a coffee pot of freshly brewed coffee on the table.
Marcus doesn't know which way of addressing people to use with each person at the table, so Lucía explains the difference to him.
Lucía: Marcus, speak to señora Odalys using usted.
Lucía: With the owner of the house or with an older person, usted shows respect.
Lucía: If she tells you to use tú with her, then you switch.
Then Lucía gives an example with a gentle question: Señora Odalys, could you serve me a little more coffee?
Yandiel, the host's grandson, comes out to the porch and asks Marcus: Hey, are you American?
Lucía: You can use tú with Yandiel, because he used tú with us first.
Lucía: Among young people, using tú shows closeness and is not a lack of respect.
Lucía gives the example: Yandiel, do you mind passing me the papaya?
Don Rigoberto, a guest of about 70, comes out of his room and sits down next to Marcus.
Lucía: An older man you call don, you also address with usted.
Marcus asks carefully: Don Rigoberto, are you from here, from Trinidad?
Don Rigoberto smiles and answers: No, I'm from Cienfuegos, but I come to this house every year.
Lucía: Now you try: ask don Rigoberto for the sugar.
Marcus: Don Rigoberto, could you pass me the sugar, please?
At the end, Marcus says to the host with a smile: I'd like another guava smoothie, if it's no trouble.

lessons.title: Coach polite and casual requests at a guesthouse
lessons.objective: Explain how to begin politely with an unfamiliar host or guest, listen for the form of address they prefer, and model a more casual request with a familiar peer.
lessons.focus: ～ていただけますか and です・ます are polite requests; ～てくれる？ is casual with a familiar peer. Japanese formality depends on relationship, setting and the other person's cues; it is not a fixed age rule. The Spanish usted/tú distinction stays as source provenance, not a literal Japanese grammar equivalence.
lessons.scene: A traveler coaches a friend through breakfast requests to a guesthouse host, a new guest and a familiar travel companion.

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 初めて会う宿の方には、まず丁寧に話しましょう。
reader.en: When meeting the guesthouse host for the first time, let's begin politely.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: どんなふうに頼めばいいですか。
reader.en: How should I ask?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 『コーヒーをもう少しいただけますか』と言えます。
reader.en: You can say, 'Could I please have a little more coffee?'

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: すみません。コーヒーをもう少しいただけますか。
reader.en: Excuse me. Could I please have a little more coffee?

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: もちろんです。私のことは名前で呼んでください。
reader.en: Of course. Please call me by my name.

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: 呼び方は相手の希望に合わせましょう。丁寧さも場面を見て調整します。
reader.en: Let's follow the person's preference for how to address them. We can adjust formality to the situation too.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 初めて会う宿泊客にはどう話しますか。
reader.en: How should I speak to a guest I have just met?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: まずは『砂糖を取っていただけますか』と丁寧に聞けます。
reader.en: You could begin by politely asking, 'Could you pass the sugar?'

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: いつもの同行者には、くだけて話してもいいですか。
reader.en: Can I speak more casually with my usual travel companion?

reader.speaker: Coach
reader.ja: お互いにそう話しているなら、『砂糖を取ってくれる？』でも自然です。
reader.en: If you already speak that way with each other, 'Could you pass the sugar?' in casual form is natural too.

speaking.partnerRole: Guesthouse host, unfamiliar guest and familiar companion
speaking.opening: 初めて会う人には、まず丁寧にお願いしましょう。
speaking.goal: Model polite requests to the host and new guest, then a casual request to a familiar companion while checking preferred forms of address.
speaking.closure: Do not infer a person's preferred address from age alone; follow their cues and the setting.
